correctness.rationale: Parity bounds all three evaluation images to the 2^{d−1} Walsh characters with |S|≡d mod2. At degree d+2, sign averaging H against the full Walsh character yields H_top=(∏_i x_i)Σ a_i x_i²; harmonicity enforces 6Σ a_i∏x_i=0, so all evaluations on cube corners vanish in this one direction. Explicit disjoint-coordinate harmonic blocks A4=u⁴−6u²v²+v⁴, B6=(231u⁶−315u⁴R²+105u²R⁴−5R⁶)/16, B7=(429u⁷−693u⁵R²+315u³R⁴−35uR⁶)/16 evaluate to nonzero multiples of 1,1,u at sign corners. The case distinctions m=d−|S| even (m=2, m=4a, m=4a+2), full S, and d=3 produce exact-degree harmonic interpolants for every other compatible Walsh character at degree d+2 and all at d,d+4. Independently checked all block Laplacians and exact Gegenbauer-Walsh eigenvalue ranks for d=3..8 (42 bounded assertions); finite evidence corroborates the explicit all-d construction.
residual_risks: The theorem concerns homogeneous harmonic polynomials of exact degree, not cumulative-degree interpolation or approximate frames.
No assertion about untested degrees or spectral singular values.

originality.rationale: Bannai–Okuda–Tagami (2013) and Zhu et al. (2015) develop harmonic-index spherical design and addition-formula methods, not full Walsh-image ranks of exact-degree solid harmonics restricted to all cube vertices. The strongly titled Bellet–Brachet–Croisille (2023) spherical-harmonic interpolation paper concerns equiangular cubed-sphere nodes on S², not the 2^d equal-sign vertices of S^{d−1}; its full body was not available here, so this difference is based on explicit geometry in its abstract, with residual reading risk. Relevant Resultary Hamming-sphere Fourier sampling results fix nonbinary shells and finite-group Fourier bands, distinct restriction operators. No inspected stronger all-degree cube-vertex harmonic-rank theorem implies the three quantified ranks.
residual_risks: One may find an equivalent character decomposition in unindexed spherical-harmonic restriction/operator literature.
The full text of Bellet et al. 2023 is subscription-previewed; only geometry, abstract and bibliographic details were inspected here.

value.rationale: The antipodally compatible data space has dimension 2^{d−1}; precisely identifying one lost full-parity Walsh mode at degree d+2 and its complete recovery at d+4 is a natural nonmonotone interpolation phenomenon in every dimension. Exact-degree harmonic sampling is important for representation theory and spherical interpolation, and the proof supplies reusable constructive interpolants rather than isolated computations.
residual_risks: Does not determine other degrees, singular values or conditioning of the interpolation operator.

final_claim: For every d≥3, exact-degree homogeneous harmonic evaluation on the 2^d normalized cube vertices has parity-compatible ranks 2^(d−1), 2^(d−1)−1 and 2^(d−1) at degrees d,d+2,d+4; only χ_[d] is lost at d+2.
limitations: Only degrees d,d+2,d+4; no conclusions about all degrees, frames or singular values.
